bundestag.summary:
SUMMARY:
This transcript details the 75th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag, held on Friday, April 24, 2026. The agenda was extensive, covering several key legislative proposals and motions. A significant portion of the session focused on energy and tax policy. Notably, the Bundestag engaged in the second and third readings of a bill to temporarily lower energy taxes on fuels, introduced by the CDU/CSU and SPD factions. Another key item was the second and third reading of a bill to amend the Electricity Tax Act and other regulations, brought forward by BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN. The session also included discussions and committee reports on motions from the AfD concerning the immediate relief of commuting workers by increasing the distance allowance and avoiding a windfall profit tax, as well as a motion from Die Linke to effectively relieve the population and economy from rising fuel prices. In conjunction with these, a motion from BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN, viewing the price shock from fossil fuels as a wake-up call to promote independence from coal, oil, and gas, was also addressed. Further legislative work involved the second and third readings of a bill to amend the Tax Consultancy Act and other tax regulations, initiated by the Federal Government. The session also included committee recommendations on motions from BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN to modernize the professional regulations for tax consultants and from Die Linke to strengthen municipal business tax revenue. Finally, the Bundestag addressed motions concerning public transportation, including a proposal from Die Linke for a nine-euro ticket to relieve private households and a proposal from BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN to amend the Public Transport Financing Act to strengthen municipalities and secure the expansion of public transport. The transcript also indicates numerous speakers from various factions, suggesting lively debate and participation.

UKRAINIAN MEN:
No discussion about Ukrainian men found in this session.
